title: Define destructive color variant in design system
description: Add red color definitions to the design system by defining CSS variables and extending the Tailwind theme configuration to support a destructive button variant.
details: First, add destructive color CSS variables to app/globals.css using HSL values that provide good contrast (e.g., --destructive: 0 84% 60%; --destructive-foreground: 210 40% 98%;). Then extend the tailwind.config.ts theme to include these colors in the destructive property. This establishes the foundation for the red button styling while maintaining consistency with the shadcn/ui design system approach.
test_strategy: Verify CSS variables are properly defined by inspecting computed styles in browser dev tools. Test that Tailwind classes like bg-destructive and text-destructive-foreground are available and render the expected red colors.

title: Add destructive variant to Button component
description: Extend the shadcn/ui Button component by adding a new 'destructive' variant to the buttonVariants configuration that uses the red color scheme.
details: Modify components/ui/button.tsx to add a 'destructive' variant to the buttonVariants object using class-variance-authority (cva). The variant should apply bg-destructive, text-destructive-foreground, and appropriate hover states (hover:bg-destructive/90). Ensure the variant follows the same pattern as existing variants and maintains proper TypeScript typing by updating the ButtonProps interface if needed.
test_strategy: Create a test component or story to render the button with variant='destructive' and verify it displays with red background and proper contrast. Test hover states and ensure no style conflicts with other variants.

title: Apply destructive variant to Create New Key button
description: Update the 'Create New Key' button implementation to use the new destructive variant, changing its appearance from blue to red.
details: Locate the 'Create New Key' button component (likely in app/dashboard/ or a related API key management page) and modify the Button component to use variant='destructive' instead of the current variant. Ensure the button text and any icons maintain proper contrast and readability. Consider adding a brief comment explaining the color choice if it deviates from typical UX patterns (since red usually indicates destructive actions).
test_strategy: Manually test the button renders with red background in both light and dark themes. Verify the button is still clickable and maintains proper accessibility standards. Use a color contrast checker to ensure WCAG AA compliance for text readability.
